source_reports.citation: Waltemeyer, S.D., 2006, Analysis of the magnitude and frequency of peak discharges for the Navajo Nation in Arizona, Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2006-5306
source_reports.version: 1.0 (no revisions listed on the pubs page)

notes: Three reports, as NSS combines them for Colorado's peak-flow statistic group (NSS region 9). (1) Capesius and Stephens, SIR 2009-5136 ver. 1.2 (April 2014; versions 1.1 and 1.2 changed Table 1 and the WLS SEPs only, and the version history states that no GLS peak-flow value changed): Mountain, Northwest, Rio Grande and Southwest regions, 8 AEPs each, from figures 3-6 (pp. 20, 22, 24, 26), which print each equation as Q = 10^b0 A^b1 ... with b0 to 2 decimals; the intercept is that printed exponent. The report's fifth (Plains) region is superseded by SIR 2016-5099 and is not stored. Ranges are the figures' 'approximate range of predictor variables'. A7500 is 'percentage of A above 7,500 feet of elevation plus 1' (figure 2 and p. 17: 1 percent is added before the log transform), stored as EL7500 (percent above 7,500 ft) with transform log10 and offset 1; its limits (0-100) are the raw percentage. S is NSS BSLDEM10M (mean basin slope, percent); P is PRECIP (mean annual precipitation, in.). Error statistics: sep_log is the printed SEP (percent) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); model_error_variance is the printed SME (standard model error, percent) converted the same way and squared. The report publishes no AVP and no covariance matrix, so intervals use sep_log. pseudo-R2 is not stored. The Northwest Q200 and Q500 equations are printed without the report's 'boxed check mark', meaning their residual plots suggest bias for some basin characteristics (pp. 18-19). (2) Kohn and others, SIR 2016-5099: Foothills and Plains hydrologic regions (eastern Colorado, split at 104 degrees W), 8 AEPs each, from figures 9 and 10 (pp. 25-26), with b0 printed to 3 decimals. Variables: A = DRNAREA, 6P100 = I6H100Y (6-hour, 100-year precipitation, in.), C = STATSCLAY (percent clay, STATSGO), Eout = OUTLETELEV (basin outlet elevation, ft), S = BSLDEM10M (mean basin slope, percent); all log10. Appendix 6 is each regression's WREG v1.05 output: model_error_variance and avp are its 'Model Error Variance' and 'Avg Variance of Prediction' (log10 units squared, 3 decimals), and the covariance is InvXLX.txt ([X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1, intercept then the variables in equation order, as printed). sep_log is the figures' SEP converted as above. Appendix 6's coefficients equal the figures' for all 16 equations; at every calibration site MEV + x'Ux reproduces WREG's printed variance of prediction, and MEV + mean x'Ux reproduces the AVP. (3) Waltemeyer, SIR 2006-5306 (Navajo Nation in AZ, UT, CO and NM): Region 8 and the High Elevation region (mean basin elevation above 7,500 ft), which NSS lists for Colorado, 7 AEPs each (2-500 years; no 200-year equation), from Table 2 (p. 7), limits from Table 1 (p. 6). Equations are printed as K x 10^n A^a ...; intercept = log10(K x 10^n). sep_log is Table 2's average standard error of prediction in log units and model_error_variance the square of its average standard error of regression in log units (the model error, p. 8). No covariance is published. S is printed as 'average basin slope, in percent', but its values (0.0231-0.4447) and the worked example (0.2422) are ft/ft, which is NSS's BSLDEM30ff ('Mean Basin Slope from 30m DEM ft/ft'); units are stored as ft/ft. Table 1 prints the region 8 elevation maximum as 7,750 with footnote 1 (pdftotext reads it as 17,750); the text on p. 6 confirms 7,750. n_sites are the per-region gage counts on p. 6 (62 and 27 of 146). Checks against the reports' own per-gage estimates: SIR 2016-5099 Appendix 5's regression estimates QP(g)r at all 187 listed gages (1,496 values) equal the stored equations at 3 significant figures. SIR 2006-5306 Appendix 1's 'predicted' lines agree for the High Elevation region (median ratio 0.996-1.002 by AEP), but for region 8 Table 2's equations give a constant fraction of them per AEP (median ratio 0.958-0.997, spread under 1%) that a refit shows to be coefficient rounding (e.g. Table 2's E exponent -2.10 against a fitted -2.094), and the region 8 2-year predicted values come from a different model with an S term (refit: 6.36e8 A^0.426 S^0.282 E^-1.74), not Table 2's Q2 = 1.08e7 A^0.457 E^-1.35. The p. 9 worked example (region 8 Q100, A 523, S 0.2422, E 6,940) prints 8,510 ft3/s, but Table 2's equation, restated in the example itself, gives 9,296. Table 2 as printed is stored, as NSS also uses it. Region codes are unique across the three reports: Mountain, Northwest, RioGrande, Southwest, Foothills, Plains, Navajo8 and NavajoHighElev. All values were double-entered (hand transcription from rendered pages vs. a programmatic parse of the PDF word boxes) with zero disagreements, and every region and AEP was cross-checked against live NSS at NSS's 3 significant figures.
